1.text: It has three or even four lamps of various sizes, which are used not only

2.text: for light, but also for cooking (Plate XV, Fig. 4).

3.text: It is usually larger than the inner room of the tents of the Reindeer

4.text: people; and among well-to-do families it may be about 30 feet in length, 10

5.text: feet in breadth, and 6 feet in height. The outer tent is also larger than

6.text: that of the Reindeer Chukchee. I saw one house which was forty feet in

7.text: diameter and had eleven stretchers to support the frame. In the outer tent,

8.text: on both sides of the sleeping-room, are placed two huge seal-skin bags, which

9.text: are used for purposes of storage.

10.text: The bottom of the sleeping-room is covered with a large walrus-hide,

11.text: forming a hard and smooth floor to tread on. The steadily burning lamps

12.text: make the room warm and dry, and even afford a chance for ventilation, which

13.text: is effected either by lifting the front or by opening a special hole in the wall,

14.text: which may be closed by a round stopper made of a piece of reindeer-skin.
